questions.topic: Seal quality tests vs leak tests
questions.question: A flexible pouch passes a seal strength test. Under USP <1207.3>, which inference is most appropriate?

options.A: It may still be defective and leak, for example with a pinhole in the pouch body, because a seal quality test provides no information on actual package integrity
options.B: It can be considered to have confirmed package integrity, because the seal quality test directly measures leak rate and can replace a subsequent leak test
options.C: It can be considered leak-free, but a leak test is still needed to quantify it and confirm the leak rate falls within the acceptable range
options.D: It indicates the seal area is completely free of defects, but other areas of the pouch must still be checked one by one with a seal quality test

questions.explanation: A seal quality test only monitors the quality and consistency of seal-related parameters and provides no information on actual package integrity, so a package that passes may still leak (for example, through a pinhole in the pouch body). Seal quality tests and leak tests must therefore be used together and cannot replace each other.

questions.question: The removal torque of a threaded closure is usually lower than its application torque. What reason does the text give?

options.A: The sealing surface of the container finish gradually wears after closure, so the force needed to open it decreases with each use
options.B: The instrument used to measure removal torque runs at a slower speed, so the initial opening force measured is lower than at application
options.C: Stress relaxation and closure back off occur over time and with environmental variables, so the sealing force gradually declines
options.D: A higher torque is deliberately applied at closure to avoid deforming the container finish, and the same force need not be maintained at opening

questions.explanation: Removal torque is lower because stress relaxation and closure back off occur over time and with environmental variables. If a closure backs off excessively during transport, storage, or distribution, the risk of leakage increases. None of the other options is a reason given in the text.
questions.reference: USP <1207.3> §2 CLOSURE APPLICATION AND REMOVAL TORQUE

questions.topic: Package burst: ASTM F2054 vs F1140
questions.question: A heat-sealed flexible pouch is to undergo package burst testing, with the goal of applying pressure uniformly to all seal areas to find the weakest seal location. Which method should be chosen?

options.A: ASTM F1140, because it does not use a restraining plate and so reflects the pressure differential challenges of sterilization cycles or distribution environments
options.B: ASTM F2054, because it uses a restraining plate to limit pouch expansion during inflation, distributing stress uniformly across the seal areas
options.C: ASTM F1140, because it does not use a restraining plate, so the pouch can expand freely and the weakest location is therefore easier to find
options.D: ASTM F2054, because it does not use a restraining plate and so directly yields measures of seal uniformity and overall package integrity

questions.explanation: F2054 uses a restraining plate to limit expansion so that stress is applied uniformly to all seals, which allows the weakest point to be found. F1140 does not use a restraining plate and is more of a snapshot of sterilization or distribution conditions, but it may fail to find the weakest spot. Moreover, a burst test itself cannot provide seal uniformity or overall integrity.

questions.question: Which statement about the residual seal force (RSF) test is correct?

options.A: It directly measures the microbial ingress risk between the aluminum cap and the vial finish, and the plastic top must be kept on during measurement to maintain the seal
options.B: It pulls the seal apart with an instrument in tension mode; a higher force means the cap is easier to open, and it is a destructive test
options.C: It measures the axial pulling force of the stopper on the vial finish; the RSF value is inversely related to crimp tightness, so a tighter crimp gives a lower value
options.D: It indirectly measures the compressive force the stopper exerts on the vial finish; RSF is linearly related to the degree of compression and can serve as an indicator of crimping process consistency

questions.explanation: RSF uses compression mode with a cap anvil to indirectly measure the force the elastomeric closure exerts on the vial finish. It is linearly and positively related to closure compression (the tighter the crimp, the higher the RSF) and does not destroy package integrity. Removing the plastic top actually gives better reproducibility.

questions.question: Airborne ultrasound is used to inspect package seals. Which best describes its principle and characteristics?

options.A: An ultrasonic signal passes through the seal area; compared with a good seal, a defective seal transmits less energy; it is non-contact and needs no coupling media
options.B: An ultrasonic signal passes through the seal area; compared with a good seal, a defective seal transmits more energy; it is non-contact and needs no coupling media
options.C: An ultrasonic signal passes through the seal area; compared with a good seal, a defective seal transmits less energy; a liquid or gel must be applied as a coupling medium
options.D: An ultrasonic signal passes through the seal area; compared with a good seal, a defective seal transmits less energy; detection results are independent of the packaging material and seal structure

questions.explanation: A poorly sealed area transmits less ultrasonic energy than a good seal. Airborne ultrasound is a non-contact technique that needs no package preparation or liquid or gel coupling media, and it is non-destructive to the package. Its detection capability does vary with the packaging material, seal structure (smooth or textured), scanning speed, and signal strength.
